shadows.name: panel-lift
shadows.purpose: Panel hover/focus-within lift, paired with color-mix border tint toward --pc.

shadows.name: track-isolation-glow
shadows.purpose: Filter on the isolated SVG track only, while its panel is hovered/focused. The one permitted glow.

shadows.name: dialog-backdrop
shadows.purpose: Near-opaque vacuum behind open guide dialogs.

motion.name: track-draw
motion.purpose: Tracks draw once from the collision core on page load (stroke-dashoffset via pathLength=1), staggered .08s per track; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: node-pop
motion.purpose: Terminal nodes fade in after their track lands (.9s–1.3s delays); disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview: The whole page is the event display of a particle detector: the ESP32-2432S028R board is the collision point at the center of layered steel detector rings, and the six firmwares are six colored particle tracks spraying out of it, each terminating at its own instrument-readout panel. Flashing a firmware once is one collision event. Everything structural — rings, rules, borders, tables — is neutral blue steel; everything that carries a signal wears that project's one committed color. The atmosphere is a near-black blue vacuum with no grid, no texture, and no decoration at rest. This world explicitly replaced and rejects the old Kraftwerk neon-schematic world: no 40px modular grid, no neon right-angle frames, no lamp-like ambient glow. Light exists only as signal response — the one-time track draw on load and the isolation highlight on hover/focus. Thai prose does the explaining in a quiet humanist voice; short English labels are machine inscriptions in tracked-caps Orbitron; every live number is a tabular Consolas readout.
keyCharacteristics: One dark vacuum ground (#070b12) with a single subtle top gradient from #0b1220; no grid, no pattern.
Steel for structure, signal color for meaning — six project colors, one per firmware, never swapped.
Instrument-readout panels: 1px steel border, 2px project-color left stripe, subgrid-aligned rows.
A hand-built SVG event display is the hero signature; panels and tracks are wired together by hover/focus isolation.
All icons are drawn inline SVG strokes; no glyph characters, no icon fonts, no raster icons.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Steel carries structure; signal color carries meaning. Any element that belongs to a project — track, stripe, icon, name, button, chip, dialog border — wears that project's exact hex, inherited via the panel's --pc custom property. Signal colors are never swapped, tinted into new roles, or used decoratively.

rules.name: The Cyan System Rule
rules.body: Lap Cyan (#05c7f2) doubles as the whole-page interaction color: links, ::selection, :focus-visible, doclinks. No second interaction color exists.

rules.name: The Amber Code Rule
rules.body: Boat Amber (#ffa02e) doubles as the color of inline code and the warning icon. Warnings are amber, never red — red belongs to CNC.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: English labels = Orbitron tracked caps; Thai content = Segoe/Noto body; live numbers = Consolas tabular. A string never borrows another voice.

rules.name: The Live Readout Rule
rules.body: Every number that comes from data (version, date) renders in Consolas with tabular-nums and is loaded live from the manifest version/updated fields — never hard-coded in markup.

rules.name: The Vacuum Rule
rules.body: Nothing glows at rest. Light — glow, lift, full-opacity color — is always a response to an event: page load (tracks draw once) or hover/focus (isolation). This is signal glow, not the banned Kraftwerk lamp glow.

dos: Do route every project-owned element through the panel's --pc custom property so dialogs, icons, buttons, and markers inherit the right signal color automatically.
Do draw every icon as inline SVG strokes (stroke currentColor or var(--pc); masked data-URI SVG for ::before icons) at icon sizes of 8–26px.
Do set every live number in Consolas tabular-nums and load it from the manifest (version, updated) at runtime.
Do keep hover economy: border tint via color-mix + one lift shadow on panels; full fill inversion on buttons; nothing else moves.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: the only animations in the system (track draw, node pop) switch off to a static fully-drawn state.
donts: Don't reintroduce the dead Kraftwerk grammar: no visible modular/40px grid, no neon right-angle frames, no ambient lamp glow at rest. Glow is permitted only as the track-isolation response.
Don't set Thai text in Orbitron, or any paragraph in Orbitron — it is for short tracked-caps English inscriptions only.
Don't use unicode glyphs or icon fonts for icons (the sole glyph exception is the ↗ external-link arrow inside Orbitron link labels).
Don't number section headings — numbers mark real sequence only (RUN 01–03).
Don't add interest/visitor counters anywhere (permanent product decision, PRODUCT.md 2026-11-05), and don't hard-code version numbers in markup.
Don't repurpose a project signal color for a new meaning, except the two committed double-duties: Lap Cyan as the system interaction color and Boat Amber as code/warning.
